chapters.title: Project Overview
chapters.markdown:
What the Project Entails

- **Project Name:** Freya -- Longform Segmentation and Transcription

- **Goal:** Accurately segment and transcribe long-form podcast audio
  recordings.

- **Audio Length:** Typically 30 minutes to over 1 hour, with multiple
  speakers.

- **Key Tasks:** Identify speakers, segment speech with timestamps,
  assign gender labels, transcribe according to guidelines, apply tags,
  evaluate audio quality.

Important Confidentiality Rules

- **DO NOT:** Take screenshots, share information, or modify contents
  outside the tool.

- **DO:** Understand NDA instructions and use secure networks.

- **Code name is Project Freya.** Do not discuss the client with anyone
  outside the project.

chapters.title: Annotation Workflow (7 Steps)
chapters.markdown:
Each task follows this structured workflow. Memorise the order.

Step 1: Review the Audio

- Listen to the recording to understand the overall conversation.

- Identify the number of speakers and note differences between voices.

- Become familiar with the flow, content, pauses, overlapping speech,
  and background sounds.

Step 2: Annotate and Label Speech

- Create timestamp intervals for each instance of speech.

- Assign the appropriate Speaker Label.

- Ensure timestamps accurately capture the beginning and end of speech.

- Annotate all audible speech.

- Handle pauses appropriately.

- Create separate segments for overlapping speakers when necessary.

- Maintain consistent speaker labels throughout the recording.

Step 3: Apply Gender Label

- Assign Male / Female / Unsure based on the perceived voice.

- The same speaker must keep the same gender label throughout the entire
  recording.

Step 4: Transcribe Speech

- Transcribe the speech inside each segment according to project
  guidelines.

- Match the speaker's words as accurately as possible.

- Follow project transcription conventions.

- Include appropriate punctuation and capitalization.

- Preserve the speaker's intended meaning.

- **Do NOT** correct grammar or rewrite the speech.

Step 5: Apply Tags

- Use tags only when additional context is needed.

- Main tags: Unsure and Truncated (see detailed rules below).

Step 6: Evaluate Audio Quality

- Assess the quality of the audio and flag any issues that affect
  transcription.

- Four options available (multiple can apply).

Step 7: Review and Submit

- Perform a final quality check of segment boundaries, speaker labels,
  gender labels, transcriptions, tags, and audio quality selections.

- Only submit after everything is accurate and complete.

chapters.title: Segmentation & Speaker Labeling Rules
chapters.markdown:
Core Segmentation Principles

- Segmentation = creating accurate timestamp intervals for when speech
  begins and ends.

- Click and drag on the spectrogram to create each segment.

- **Timestamp boundaries must begin and end within 500 milliseconds** of
  actual speech boundaries.

- **Annotate all audible speech** (including any language).

Handling Pauses (Critical Rule)

- **Pause under 2 seconds (less than 2,000 ms):** Keep the speech in the
  **same segment**.

- **Pause over 2 seconds (greater than 2,000 ms):** Create a **new
  segment**.

*Example: If the same speaker pauses for 1.5 seconds then continues,
keep it as one interval.*

Overlapping Speech

- Create separate segments for each speaker.

- Timestamp intervals are allowed to overlap.

- Ensure each segment is assigned to the correct speaker.

Laughter and Interjections

- Standalone laughter and interjections (Oh, Wow, Hmm, Uh-huh, Laughter)
  must get their own timestamp interval + the correct tag.

- Laughter is marked using the [laughter] tag (not written as "haha").

Assigning Speaker Turns

- Assign Speaker Turn numbers in the order speakers first appear in the
  recording.

- Each speaker gets their own track.

- **Once assigned, the same speaker must keep the same number throughout
  the entire recording.**

- Use the + button to create a new Speaker Turn when a new person
  appears.

When Speaker Identity Is Unclear

- Review the surrounding conversation for context.

- Use your best judgment.

- Select the most likely existing Speaker Turn.

- **Do NOT create a new Speaker Turn simply because you are uncertain.**

Gender Labels

- After assigning Speaker Turns, apply Male / Female / Unsure.

- Same speaker must retain the same gender label for the entire
  recording.

chapters.title: Transcription Guidelines
chapters.markdown:
Core Goal

Transcribe **exactly what the speaker says**. Do **not** correct
grammar, improve wording, or rewrite the speech.

Do's

- Capture the speech as spoken

- Preserve the speaker's intended meaning

- Follow project conventions

- Apply proper punctuation and capitalization so it is readable

Don'ts

- Do not rewrite or improve the speaker's wording

- Do not correct grammar or sentence structure

Disfluencies -- Use the Unsure Tag

**Filled pauses (Eh, Er, Um):**

- Wrap them in an Unsure tag.

- If multiple filled pauses occur consecutively, use a single tag.

- *Examples: [unsure: er] how can I explain* or *[unsure: eh er um]*

**Stuttering:**

- Transcribe the stuttered portion to the best of your ability and wrap
  it in an Unsure tag.

- *Example: [unsure: absolu] absolutely*

**Fragmented / cut-off words:**

- Transcribe the fragmented portion and wrap it in an Unsure tag.

- *Example: Barack Obama the [unsure: presi]*

Additional Keep-in-Mind Rules

- If an utterance is largely unintelligible or nonsensical → use an
  empty Unsure tag.

- Entire utterances in the wrong language → leave blank + empty Unsure
  tag.

- If a punctuation mark cannot be transcribed with certainty → apply the
  Unsure tag to the punctuation symbol.

- When transcribing from scratch, use the first accepted spelling from
  the official dictionary for your locale.

When You May Skip a Recording

- A person is being recorded without their knowledge, or

- The audio is fully non-transcribable.

**Do not skip recordings for any other reason.**

chapters.title: Tags (Unsure & Truncated)
chapters.markdown:
How to Apply Tags

- **Only use the tool controls** (highlight the word or empty space →
  click the tag).

- **Never type tags manually** into the transcription field.

Unsure Tag

Apply when speech cannot be transcribed with certainty.

- Speech is mumbled or difficult to understand

- Audio distortion, interference, or volume issues affect
  intelligibility

- A word or phrase cannot be transcribed with certainty

- Foreign words cannot be transcribed confidently

- Made-up words are present

- Filled pauses, stuttering, or fragmented words make the intended
  speech unclear

- Entire utterance is largely unintelligible or in the wrong language →
  empty Unsure tag

Truncated Tag

Apply when speech is **clearly cut off by the recording**.

**Use Truncated when:**

- The initial word(s) of the track is/are cut by the system

- The ending word(s) of the track is/are cut by the system

- The recording starts or ends before the speaker finishes speaking

- The first or last words of the audio are truncated AND too unclear to
  transcribe

**Do NOT apply Truncated when:**

- A final sound or consonant is unclear, but there is no evidence that
  speech was cut off

- A sound at the beginning or end may simply be non-speech noise

- A word can be clearly understood, even if you suspect the speaker
  intended a longer version

- The speaker's words are complete (even if it sounds like they might
  continue)

**PRIORITY RULE: If both Truncated and Unsure appear to apply → use
Truncated.**

chapters.title: Audio Quality Evaluation
chapters.markdown:
There are four options. Multiple options may apply to the same
recording.

1. Unclear Audio

Select when audio quality prevents you from confidently transcribing all
or part of the speech.

- Background noise

- Speech masked by noise

- Audio distortion

- Whispering that cannot be confidently transcribed

- Singing that cannot be confidently transcribed

2. Heavy Accent

Select when a speaker's accent or dialect makes it difficult to
confidently understand and transcribe what is said.

- Also apply the Unsure tag to the affected portions of speech.

- If the speech can still be transcribed confidently despite the accent,
  do not select this option.

- Does not apply to babbling, cooing, or unclear child speech.

3. Incorrect Language

Select when an entire utterance is spoken in a language that differs
from the locale being evaluated.

- Do not attempt to transcribe the utterance, even if you understand the
  language.

- Use an empty Unsure tag and leave the transcription blank.

- If you have reason to believe the entire utterance could be in another
  language, select Incorrect Language.

4. Synthesized or Recorded Speech

Select when speech is generated, recorded, or artificially altered
(voice assistants, synthesized voices, voice filters).

- This option applies only to directed speech and does not apply to
  background noise.

- If altered speech cannot be transcribed confidently → apply an empty
  Unsure tag and select both Synthesized/Recorded Speech and Unclear
  Audio.

chapters.title: Pre-Annotated Tasks & Forbidden Zones
chapters.markdown:
Pre-Annotated Tasks

Some tasks already contain annotations when opened. You must review and
verify everything before submission.

**Your Responsibilities:**

1.  **Verify Timestamp Intervals --** Ensure boundaries are accurate
    (within 500 ms). Adjust if speech starts earlier or ends later.

2.  **Verify Speaker Labels --** Confirm the label matches the correct
    speaker and remains consistent. Fix inconsistencies.

3.  **Correct Inconsistencies --** Update annotations so they accurately
    reflect the audio.

4.  **Remove Invalid Segments --** Delete any pre-annotated segment that
    contains only silence or background noise.

Forbidden Zones

- **Gradable Zone:** The section you are responsible for annotating.

- **Forbidden Zone (usually red):** Visible for context but cannot be
  modified.

**Only the gradable zone should be annotated.**

**Handling Speech Across Zone Boundaries:**

  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
             **Scenario**                         **Action**

   Speech falls entirely within the    Annotate and transcribe normally
             gradable zone            

   Speech extends into the gradable   Annotate and transcribe the ENTIRE
                 zone                               segment

    Speech falls entirely within a    Do NOT create, edit, or modify the
            forbidden zone                          segment

   You only need the forbidden zone   Use it for reference only -- do not
              for context                          modify it
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------

chapters.title: Final Review Checklist
chapters.markdown:
Use this checklist before every submission.

Segmentation

- [ ] All speech has been segmented

- [ ] Timestamp boundaries are accurate (within 500 ms)

- [ ] Overlapping speech has been handled correctly

Speaker Labels

- [ ] Speaker labels are accurate

- [ ] Labels remain consistent throughout the recording

- [ ] Gender labels have been assigned correctly

Transcription

- [ ] Transcriptions match the speech

- [ ] Project transcription conventions have been followed

- [ ] Proper punctuation and capitalization have been applied

Tags and Audio Quality

- [ ] Tags have been applied correctly

- [ ] Audio quality issues have been identified accurately

- [ ] All applicable audio quality options have been selected

Pre-Annotations

- [ ] Existing annotations have been verified

- [ ] Invalid segments have been corrected or removed

chapters.title: Key Recap -- Critical Rules to Remember
chapters.markdown:
- Follow the annotation workflow consistently from review through
  submission.

- Create accurate speech segments; timestamp boundaries must align
  within 500 ms of speech.

- **Pause \< 2 s → same segment. Pause \> 2 s → new segment.**

- Maintain consistent Speaker Turn and gender labels throughout each
  recording.

- Transcribe speech accurately; do not correct grammar or rewrite.

- Use Truncated and Unsure tags appropriately. If both apply → Truncated
  wins.

- Identify and report audio quality issues using the correct categories.

- Review pre-annotated tasks carefully and correct inaccuracies.

- Annotate only within the gradable zone. Never edit forbidden zones.

- Perform a thorough final quality review before submitting.

- **When guidelines conflict, the Longform Segmentation and
  Transcription guidelines take precedence over the general
  Transcription Conventions.**

chapters.title: Knowledge Check Questions & Answers
chapters.markdown:
These are the exact knowledge-check questions from the interactive
course. Memorise the correct answers.

1. What should you do when a pause is less than 2,000 milliseconds?

**Correct Answer: Keep the same segment**

*Rule:* Pause \< 2 s → same segment. Pause \> 2 s → new segment.

2. What should you do if a speech segment falls entirely within a
forbidden zone?

**Correct Answer: Do not create or modify the segment**

*Rule:* Forbidden zones are for context only. Never annotate or edit
inside them.

3. When should the Heavy Accent audio quality option be selected?

**Correct Answer: When an accent affects transcription**

*Rule:* Only select it when the accent makes confident transcription
difficult. Do not select it just because an accent is present.

4. A word cannot be understood because it is masked by background
noise. Which tag should be applied?

**Correct Answer: Unsure**

*Rule:* Use the Unsure tag whenever speech cannot be transcribed with
confidence (noise, distortion, mumbling, etc.).

5. Which tag should be used when speech is clearly cut off by the
recording?

**Correct Answer: Truncated**

*Rule:* Use Truncated when speech is clearly cut off at the start or end
of the recording.

6. How should overlapping speech be handled?

**Correct Answer: Create separate segments for each speaker**

*Rule:* Create separate segments for each speaker. Overlapping
timestamps are allowed.

7. When reviewing a pre-annotated segment that contains only silence,
what should you do?

**Correct Answer: Delete the segment**

*Rule:* Remove any pre-annotated segment that contains only silence or
background noise.

8. A speech segment starts within a forbidden zone and ends within the
gradable zone. What should you do?

**Correct Answer: Label and transcribe the segment in full**

*Rule:* If the segment extends into the gradable zone, annotate and
transcribe the entire segment.

9. A word is both truncated by the recording and masked by background
noise. What should you do?

**Correct Answer: Apply the Truncated tag and select Unclear Audio**

*Rule:* Truncated takes priority over Unsure. Also select the Unclear
Audio quality option because of the noise.

10. How should laughter be represented in a transcription?

**Correct Answer: Marked using the [laughter] tag**

*Rule:* Standalone laughter gets its own timestamp and is marked with
the Laughter tag (not written as "haha").

11. A speaker pauses for 1.5 seconds mid-sentence, then continues. What
should you do?

**Correct Answer: Keep it within the same segment**

*Rule:* 1.5 seconds is less than 2 seconds → keep in the same segment.

12. Which tag takes precedence when both Truncated and Unsure appear to
apply?

**Correct Answer: Truncated**

*Rule:* Truncated always takes priority over Unsure.

- Exam name: Freya -- Live Transcription EDC

- Attempts allowed: 2

- Required score: 90%

chapters.title: Live exam answers (22)
chapters.markdown:
**FREYA CERTIFICATION EXAM**

Questions & Correct Answers

Compiled from the Live Transcription EDC exam (22 questions) • Based on
official guidelines

**Note:** Answers follow the Freya Longform Segmentation & Transcription
guidelines and the interactive course knowledge checks. Passing score is
90%.

1\. What should you do if the voice speaks only half of a word and
doesn't correct it?

**Answer: Type the part of the word spoken with [unsure] label.**

2\. What is the maximum allowed timing deviation at the start or end of
the speech?

**Answer: 0.5 seconds**

3\. Which of the following is correct?

*Options included:*

• The number of speakers equals the number of intervals.

• The speaker ID is determined by the order in which speakers speak. The
first speaker is speaker1, the second is speaker2, and each speaker has
only one ID.

**Answer: The speaker ID is determined by the order in which speakers
speak. The first speaker is speaker1, the second is speaker2, and each
speaker has only one ID.**

4\. If a speaker is interrupted by another speaker's response (such as
"um" or "ah") and then continues, should the content before and after
the interruption be placed in two separate intervals?

**Answer: Yes**

5\. Can you apply Truncated and Unsure labels to the same words?

**Answer: No, use only Truncated for that case.**

6\. If the speaker laughs during the speech, how should you annotate
that?

**Answer: [laughter]**

7\. Can non-speech sounds or disfluencies be included in the segments?

**Answer: Yes, but only if the sound or disfluence is in the middle of
the speech, and the speech continues afterwards.**

8\. If two people are clearly heard speaking at the same time, how
should you label it?

**Answer: 1 speaker label per person.**

9\. What should you do if a pre-annotated segment only has silence?

**Answer: Delete the segment.**

10\. Regarding the [truncated] label, which of the following is
correct? (Select all that apply)

• Use [truncated] label only when the first or last word of the audio
is truncated AND cannot be transcribed.

• Do not use [truncated] label if the last word of a sentence is
audible and understandable in context (without obvious evidence of
truncation).

• Do not use [truncated] label if the speaker speaks in complete
sentences, even if it sounds like the speaker might have said more after
the audio ends.

**Answer: All three options are correct.**

11\. Which of the following is correct?

*Options included statements about synthesized speech, heavy accent on
babbling, foreign language, and unclear audio with noise.*

**Answer: If the speaker's language is synthesized but audible, "request
is synthesized or recorded speech" should still be selected.**

12\. When should you use the Truncated label? (Select all that apply)

• When a word is half pronounced in the middle of the speech.

• When the speaker stutters and says half of a word.

• When the audio starts with a cut word.

• When the audio ends with a half word.

**Answer: When the audio starts with a cut word. + When the audio ends
with a half word.**

13\. What is the maximum length of a pause on the speech that can be
included in one segment?

**Answer: 2 seconds**

14\. If the interval is "hmm right", which of the following is the
correct transcription?

**Answer: Hmm, right.**

15\. Which labels will be used in this task? (Select all that apply)

*Options: [wrong language], [laughter], [noise], [truncated],
[unsure]*

**Answer: [laughter] • [truncated] • [unsure]**

16\. What should you do when there is a long part of the utterance in a
foreign language?

**Answer: Label it as [unsure] and leave it empty.**

17\. If you encounter a sequence of filled pauses, you should...

**Answer: Use one [unsure] label for all the consecutive filled
pauses.**

18\. When a segment begins or ends in a Forbidden zone you should:

**Answer: Annotate the whole segment normally.**

19\. If the voice speaking does grammar mistakes during the speech, when
annotating it you should:

**Answer: Annotate everything just the way the speaker said it.**

20\. If you have a segment like "Who won the Wor World Cup this year?",
which way would be the correct way to annotate it?

**Answer: Who won the [unsure: Wor] World Cup this year?**

21\. What if the pre-transcribed text is missing filled pauses or
stutters?

**Answer: Add them if possible and tag these words with an [unsure]
tag.**

22\. How should you annotate filled pauses?

**Answer: [unsure]**

*--- End of Exam Q&A Compilation ---*

All answers are based on the official Freya guidelines. Use for personal
review only.
